title: Java Write to Files
learningObjectives: Write text to a file with FileWriter.
Use try-with-resources to close a writer reliably.
Append content without replacing existing content.
Understand character encoding and IOException concerns.
Verify written text by reading it back.

understand.concept: Java's FileWriter writes character data to a file. Opening it in the default mode replaces existing content; the constructor with append=true adds content to the end. Writers should be closed so buffered characters are flushed. Try-with-resources closes the writer automatically, including when an exception occurs. For explicit character encodings in modern applications, prefer Files.newBufferedWriter with a StandardCharsets value.
understand.whyItMatters: Writing files allows applications to save reports, settings and generated text. Correct resource management prevents lost buffered data and open handles, while explicit character encoding keeps text predictable across different machines.
understand.analogy: Think of a path as a labeled address to a storage location; the address and the data stored there are different things.
understand.analogyLimit: A path is not a guarantee that the target exists or that the program has permission to access it.

explain.narrative:
## Character writers and file contents

A `Writer` writes character data. `FileWriter` is a character-output stream connected to a file. Its one-argument constructor opens the file for writing and replaces existing contents; the constructor with `append=true` adds characters at the end. Calling `write` does not mean every character has already reached storage because writers may buffer data.

## Close resources reliably

Use try-with-resources so the writer is closed automatically when the block exits, including when an exception occurs. Closing flushes buffered characters and releases the resource. Do not rely on the program ending to close an open writer.

## Choose a character set

The traditional FileWriter constructors use the platform default charset. If a file format requires a known encoding, prefer `Files.newBufferedWriter(path, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)` or another explicit charset. Use the same encoding when the file is read later.

## Replace versus append

Choose replace mode when generating a complete new version of a file. Choose append mode for logs or records that should be added without removing earlier text. Be explicit: accidental replace mode can destroy existing content.

## Error handling and safe output

Writing may fail because a directory is missing, permission is denied, storage is unavailable or the path is invalid. Handle `IOException` and report failure to the caller. Write only to an application-controlled destination; never build a destination path by blindly concatenating untrusted input.

examples.title: Write text
examples.explanation: write sends characters to the writer, and closing it flushes them before reading the file.

examples.title: Append text
examples.explanation: The append constructor preserves existing content and writes new characters at the end.

examples.title: Write multiple lines
examples.explanation: A newline character separates the two written lines in the file.

examples.title: Write UTF-8 explicitly
examples.explanation: Files.newBufferedWriter accepts an explicit charset for predictable text encoding.

examples.title: Replace existing content
examples.explanation: The one-argument FileWriter constructor truncates an existing file before writing.

practise.guidedTask: Write `First line` and `Second line` to a file using Files.newBufferedWriter with UTF-8 and try-with-resources. Read the file back with Files.readString using UTF-8 and print it. Then append `Third line` in a separate writer and verify the complete contents.
practise.independentTask: Create a simple text-based activity log. It must write a header in replace mode only when starting a new log, append later events, use UTF-8 explicitly, close every writer with try-with-resources and report IOException. Test first-run creation, a second append and a line containing non-ASCII text.
hints: Use Files.newBufferedWriter with StandardCharsets.UTF_8 when the encoding must be predictable.
Choose replace or append options deliberately; append preserves existing text while replace truncates it.
Use try-with-resources to close and flush the writer, then read back with the same charset to verify the result.
practise.challenge: Design a safe log-writing method that does not accidentally truncate an existing log. Explain how you handle a missing parent directory, an I/O failure and concurrent writers. State whether your design guarantees atomic writes; do not claim atomicity unless you implement and verify it.

questions.prompt: Which class writes character data to a file?
questions.explanation: FileWriter is a character stream writer for text files.

questions.prompt: How do you append with FileWriter?
questions.explanation: The append flag preserves existing content and writes new text at the end.

questions.prompt: Why use try-with-resources for a writer?
questions.explanation: try-with-resources closes an AutoCloseable resource at the end of the block.

questions.prompt: What does the one-argument FileWriter constructor do to existing content?
questions.explanation: The default FileWriter mode truncates existing file content.

questions.prompt: How can an application select UTF-8 explicitly?
questions.explanation: This API makes the chosen text encoding explicit and avoids platform-default charset differences.
